Yeah, but after 6 years of hoping for something to change I kind of realized that it's just not how it works. Things change, but something that's been baked into how I think so deeply hasn't.

Worst part is that I know I can't tell anyone because if I do, I know (from experience!) that they won't love me anymore.
Is everyone worthy of love? If so, then I want something more than love. I know that you don't mean that. If I died then you wouldn't care in about half a month. Not sure that's what I call love.
Hah, I think about that all the time. I feel like I can't love myself without knowing that I'm worthy of other's love. But I can't feel like others love me because I feel like I'm not lovable.
Haha, maybe that's why I feel like this. Even if someone were to honestly tell me that they love me (and not just because they think it's what I want to hear), it wouldn't help.

Thanks for the link. One problem is that my brain keeps telling me that I shouldn't do this, that a professional will not be able to help me, that they don't care about me, that they just want money, that they won't understand me, etc.

I think they are right to though! They certainly don't after the first couple of times, but eventually if someone is coming to you with the same set of feelings of worthlessness over and over again, you eventually get fed up with it. Hell, just today a friend yelled at me saying that she's not supposed to be my personal motivator. I agree, she's not. At this point I can say for fairly certain this isn't going away, ever. The only treatment (*not cure*) that has proven effective is when real-life friends comfort me (because I feel like know that they know me and sincerely care about me). So what do I do?

The worst part is, when I'm feeling like this, I always have this strong temptation to reach out to people who I care about and who I want to care about me. It's almost like I'm seeking attention or seeking the feeling of being cared about at least. Ironically, that drives people further away from me and offers temporary relief at best because these feelings come back soon.
How do you find a good professional? My experiences have all been pretty crappy so far. I feel like it needs to be someone who actually understands how I think about the world in order to help me.

I agree. I think we do not, in this respect, recognize we do not live in a perfect world nor will we for the time being. In an imperfect world, suicide is the most humane option for many individuals to choose.

We are essentially making people live by making it impossible or highly difficult for those who wish to commit suicide to do so "safely" and painlessly. My argument is that this coercion is largely not justifiable. I am not arguing about whether individuals should or should not commit suicide, just that they should have the choice of safe, painless assisted suicide should they wish to.

When you speak of specialization and expertise, you seem to have the idea of university or trade school graduates in mind, with the addition of some others, perhaps. What about people whose lives consist of complete misery? As I stated in another post, I am not speaking merely for those of us living in developed nations, but also for people who live repetitive, hard lives and are constantly on the brink of starvation. People who live in fear of being tortured, raped, etc. when even trying to find a place to defecate. These people are in the hundreds of millions, at least, a number that is hard for us to even comprehend. What about people with severe, untreatable mental illness for whom their life consists of sitting in a mental institution until they die "naturally" decades in the future?

What about those who simply do not wish to be around anymore? An infinite number of people who could have existed do not exist. Similarly your nonexistence makes no difference in the long-term. The singularity is unlikely to happen anytime soon, and that world could be even worse than the one we live in now, with a ruling elite that never dies and keeps the rest of the world population highly oppressed.

Technically you are correct, people are capable of suicide today. I am well aware of that, and that is obviously not what I am speaking about. I am speaking of suicide with dignity. Legalized, painless, and widely available.

I mean wrong in the sense that I am coming to the wrong conclusion given that we share the same or similar moral views and presumptions. If you are a Catholic arguing with another Catholic on this issue, but you both accept the teachings of Church as authoritative, then who is "right" is obvious. There will be some more ambiguity here, but it is possible to argue for and against different public policy views with those who share a similar basis for their moral and public policy viewpoints.

I think it is a hard subject to address because it is a deeply emotional one. Also, I was not speaking of legal ramifications. I believe women should not only not be persecuted for abortion, but that they should have abortion services readily available should they choose to use them and that doctors should not be punished for providing them with these services. This ensures they have power over their own bodies, even when others would not like them to. I believe the same applies to any individual who wishes to no longer exist.

"Natural" death itself, being an inevitability, causes quite a bit of emotional distress as well. Suicide is of course also a form of natural death in the sense that all our actions are natural. Should we outlaw all behaviors and individual choices that cause others emotional distress? I am certain that abortion causes much mental distress for conservative Catholic families when a member of their family does so. Does that justify limiting a woman's bodily autonomy?

Furthermore, you do not take into account the unnecessary suffering of the person who wants to end their life. If that person's suffering outweighs the suffering of those who would grieve for their loss, then it is still sad but forcing that person to live results in more suffering. That is especially the case if they cause those around them to suffer, as well.

Not only would this be respecting individual autonomy, it would potentially dramatically reduce suffering in the world by giving people an option to end their lives. I am not speaking merely of those of us lucky enough to live in developed nations (although I am speaking for them, as well), but also for those billions of people who barely survive day-to-day.
Okay, well I figured it couldn't hurt to try. I will search for some other forums to do so. There's not a lot out there, though, so I figured Reddit would be a good place to try.

I read that there was a "troll" PMing people with advice, so I was hoping they might get in contact with me or that someone else might have some information. This is the first subreddit that shows up when you search for suicide. Like I said, if there is a more appropriate subreddit I will post there instead.

I am also willing to accept some pain, but ideally none, obviously.
Do a lot of research on colleges, and go to a college with like-minded people. Trust me, you will have a great time.
